_comment: ADR-096 class policy — the router-owned half of model routing (the per-stack candidate CHAINS stay in agents/stacks.json / AgentStack claims; launchers pass them to POST /route, the router filters against THIS file + strikes + capacity). Lives in the kustomize dir because kustomize configMapGenerator cannot load outside its root; consumers use the API, never this file directly. tier_thresholds (per rail, in the `rails:` block) = FU-109 (dispatch units defer later than heavy sessions). the `models` table must cover every stacks.json chain entry (CI: devbox run router-self-test + agents-registration-lint). rotation_fallback IS the FU-095 rotation v1 — no rankings API exists (probed 2026-07-27), so the list is git-curated, fed by the weekly scout digest; entries are chain-TAIL candidates only, graduation into heads stays human. provider_policy (FU-186): per-class key; absent = today's pin behaviour (provider.order injected). "exacto" skips pin injection — the completion path appends :exacto to the served model id, which the proxy forwards UNTOUCHED with the M4 pin skipped, letting upstream's tool-call-quality ordering own provider selection. Priced classes carry no policy by construction. `rails` is written in the CANONICAL rail vocabulary (Goal #1769 acceptance 1) — `anthropic-subscription` | `opencode-go` | `openrouter` | `opencode-zen` — the same names `model_id.parse()` produces and every decision row echoes; the router derives a candidate's rail from that parser and gates it on ITS OWN rail's capacity (a Go candidate on /opencode-limit, never on the OpenRouter key's state). The pre-Goal-#1769 spelling (`subscription`) still loads through a one-release alias in router.py:RAIL_ALIASES and is deleted next release. CALLER CAPABILITY (Goal #1769 acceptance 4, router half, 2026-09-22): a candidate is filtered by what the CALLER can ride, not only by what the account can buy — `/route` takes the caller's `surface` (claude-cli | opencode-cli | openai-api) and its `key_ref`, and a candidate whose rail needs a fact the caller did not send is skipped `caller:no-key_ref` (openrouter) or `caller:surface` (anthropic-subscription / opencode-go / opencode-zen) BEFORE any capacity gate is consulted. Sending NEITHER fact filters nothing, so an un-adopted caller walks exactly as before. The requirement table is the `rails:` block below (Goal #1769 acceptance 2 externalized router.py's RAIL_SURFACE into it).

rails._comment: Goal #1769 acceptance 2 — the ONE declared table of rail facts. Before this, a rail's gate/cost/windows/thresholds/concurrency lived as scattered env constants (OPENCODE_MAX_RUNNING, ANTHROPIC_UTIL_THRESHOLD_*) and an Anthropic-only top-level tier_thresholds; a rail we chose not to use was simply OMITTED. Now every rail is DECLARED, and one we do not use is declared `enabled: false` with its reason (Zen). PRECEDENCE — two authorities, two skip reasons: `enabled: false` in git is `rail:disabled` and CANNOT be overridden from env; OPENCODE_RAIL_DISABLED (the FU-213 env kill switch, openrouter-proxy.py) is `rail:parked` and beats `enabled: true` — a kill switch beats a git round-trip. `gate` names the capacity probe the /route walk consults (sub | go | or | none); `surfaces` is the caller surfaces the rail serves (acceptance 4's predicate reads THIS, not an in-router table); `cost` is flat-window | flat-pool | per-token; `windows` are the utilization windows the gate reads; `tier_thresholds` is the per-rail FU-109 table (the Anthropic-only top-level table is retired — a stale file's copy is folded in once at load by router.py:_migrate_tier_thresholds); `concurrency` is the rail's bound (the Go rail's OPENCODE_MAX_RUNNING is now the ENV OVERRIDE of this declared value, not its only home).

opencode-zen._reason: reachable and unmetered: pay-per-token USD with no pricing table, no spend meter, no ledger bucket — ledger.py:_model_rail folds it into "openrouter"; un-parking rides FU-170 (b)+(c), not this Goal.

coding._comment: chain_head added 2026-09-19 (operator ruling — the FOURTH stand-in of the goal-decompose 08-23 / dispatch 08-25 / review 09-03 class, codified at the third). It REPLACES the fleet's last per-stack chain — the platform claim's workerModel deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash:exacto + workerModelFallbacks [claude/haiku] — which Goal #1640 acceptance 6 (#1782) drops when the claim goes chainless at routerMode: authoritative. It EXISTS because chain_source: "stack" then resolves nothing and the served walk draws straight from the ranked rotation, leaving the operator's ordering (v4-flash first, v4.1-flash next) stated nowhere — the identical failure each of the three prior heads was added to fix. Entries are BARE ids on purpose: provider_policy: "exacto" below appends the suffix at serve time, so a pre-suffixed entry would double it. Retires with the P4 flip, like the other three heads.

review._comment: chain_head added 2026-09-03 (the THIRD instance of the goal-decompose 08-23 / dispatch 08-25 class, codified per the >=2 rule): on chainless stacks chain_source resolves nothing, so the served walk drew the cheapest ROTATION model for reviews — xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 [market], 44+9 of 55 review decisions in the 24h shadow read — while the doctrine (review = the safety net, sonnet-class, model-routing.md M10) was carried only by the FU-188 incident pin's fallback in reviewer-session.sh. The head makes the served decision say what the lane actually runs; rails stay subscription-first with the rotation as capacity failover. SUBTRACTION (Goal #1769 acceptance 4, router half, 2026-09-22): the "second rail entry is a foot-gun" caveat this field used to carry is RETIRED — the walk now filters candidates on CALLER CAPABILITY (a rail whose credential the caller did not send, or whose CLI surface it cannot execute, is skipped `caller:*` BEFORE any capacity gate), so listing openrouter as a failover is safe by construction and no longer depends on the FU-188 shadow pin. Retires with the P4 flip like the other two heads.

dispatch._comment: chain_head added 2026-08-25 (operator ruling — the goal-decompose 08-23 precedent, second instance of the same class): the coordinator-lane /route calls (coordinator, dispatch-unit, responder) arrive stack-less, so chain_source resolves nothing and the rotation universe is all-OpenRouter — with rails subscription-only the served walk exhausted on EVERY call (123 chain-exhausted defers over 7d, homelab#775 comment 5415278592) while the launchers' fail-open fallbacks silently carried the lane on sonnet. claude/sonnet matches the carried behavior (coordination judgment default). Both chain_head stand-ins retire when the P4 flip promotes the M11 ladder's subscription candidate into the served walk.

goal-decompose._comment: M10 goal-lane reasoning class — goal-decompose/goal-checkpoint items ride the subscription rail's reasoning tier. Replaces the launcher-side case map (PR#801); consumed by coordinator-session.sh calling resolve-model.sh with --class goal-decompose. chain_head added 2026-08-23 (operator ruling, G-B launch): WITHOUT it the class had no candidates and every live call deferred chain-exhausted — the launcher fallback (GOAL_MODEL:-opus) silently carried the lane while the fixture's stub router masked it. claude/fable is deliberate: the design-agents corpus has only ever been written/read by fable, and the decompose is the load-bearing corpus read (in-cluster fable smoke passed 2026-08-23, FABLE-OK through the proxy /anthropic leg). Revisit to opus only on an ATTENDED opus-vs-fable decomposition comparison, measured by authoring-attributable rounds (the miss-ledger metric).

regular._comment: ADR-104 research BANDS — four classes whose only job is to select a curated pool below (`class` + `slot` + `jitter:false` = the draw verb). They carry no chain: a draw never falls through to the rotation path, because a substituted arm is a corrupted experiment (§M13).

pools._comment: ADR-104 / model-routing-history.md §M13 — the CURATED half of the research draw verb: ranked, family-deduped, disjoint bands, consumed by slot index and never computed at request time. HAND-SEEDED (FU-162, 2026-08-11): entries are `models` members only (the human-approved universe — graduation stays human) and the ranking is that grade, large → cheap → free, because this pod has no capability/market read. The scout's weekly refresh (capability × task_market × effective price × rail-compat, §M7 leg 5) replaces the ranking and deepens the bands — it rides FU-161, so until then this table moves by PR and `version` bumps with every edit to the bands. `version` is echoed by /route as pool_version: an arm table that records (class, slot, pool_version) can be re-drawn exactly. Disjointness + family-dedup are CURATION policy, not router invariants (ADR-104 (3)) — devbox run router-self-test is where they are enforced, at edit time. Known shortfall: `regular` is 6 deep against the doc's 7-arm over-provision, and `instrument` shares the deepseek FAMILY with regular's #2 (the run-1 slip was the same MODEL grading its own arm, which disjointness forbids); both are curation depth, i.e. the scout refresh's job.

urgency_map._comment: M11 leg 2 (homelab#159): urgency is a DISPATCH property, resolved deterministically and never inferred from the prompt (ADR-094) — which is why the table lives here beside label_map rather than in any model. Precedence in /route: the caller's explicit `urgency` field wins (it is the only input that can carry round STATE — 'this round is a ci-red retry', 'this child has an assembly waiting' — which no label spells), then these labels (tight wins a tie), then the role, then `default`. The launcher/scan reads the SAME table when it supplies the field, so the two sides cannot drift.

ladder._comment: M11 (homelab#159) cross-rail cost ladder, SHADOW-only today: rungs free → subscription → paid, ordered by TRUE MARGINAL cost. subscription_model is the rail's stand-in candidate when a chain names no claude/* entry (same constant as the §M12 degrade, AGENT_SUBSCRIPTION_FALLBACK_MODEL). promote_after = banked clean runs at the start rung before the cell tries one rung cheaper; tight_floor_tier = the rung tight work starts at until the cell has PROVEN the free rung. The subscription rung is only ever priced ~0 while the FU-088 gates (429 latch, per-window utilization, semaphore) are all clear — the safety net's slots are not the ladder's to spend.

cooldown._comment: ADR-096 addendum 4: model-level temporary blacklist. Trip when >= min_events in window_s and the non-2xx share >= bad_share (reason = dominant class); hold base_s doubling per consecutive trip up to max_s; ANY 2xx clears + resets the streak (half-open recovery: an expired hold makes the model eligible again and cheapest-effective ordering re-picks it — natural traffic is the probe). Keyed on OUR passive events, never upstream uptime (laguna measured 100% upstream while 81% 429 for our account, 2026-08-02).
cooldown._comment_pair: Goal #1640 acceptance 5 (router half): the (model, provider) PAIR cooldown. A SEPARATE, coarser mechanism from the transport belt above — keyed (model, provider), tripped by >= pair_min_tasks DISTINCT tasks striking the pair with a SERVING_CLASSES class inside pair_window_s, held pair_base_s doubling per streak up to pair_max_s, and cleared ONLY by a clean ride (a run_report with outcome 'pr'), never by a 2xx. State is the existing strikes table (no new table): the hold is derived from the pair's distinct-task strike set, and a clean ride after the last strike refutes it. Expiry is half-open — the pair is eligible again and a strike during half-open doubles the hold. Durations are the operator's numbers as recorded on the Goal (6 h doubling to 7 d).

circuit_breaker._comment: ADR-096 addendum 3: in-flight 4XX breaker per (session, model). auth (401/403) trips fast — an auth failure never self-heals mid-session (the 140-401 laguna:free storm); generic 4xx gets more rope; 429 NEVER counts (fail-over/back-off, not session-abort). hold_s = how long forwarding stays stopped.

selection._comment: The /route ordering rule (operator 2026-07-27, built in P3): among same-class/same-tier candidates the EFFECTIVE-cheapest wins, with a small randomization — a uniform pick among candidates within jitter_band_pct of the cheapest — so evidence keeps accruing across near-priced models instead of a monoculture. Price basis order (ADR-096 addendum 2): MARKET effective price (frontend stats/effective-pricing — 30d traffic-weighted, real cache rates; same basis the pins use) → harvested /generation billed costs as the cross-check → registry list-blend as cold-start fallback.

models._comment: Goal #1769 acceptance 3 — the ONE per-model table, keyed CANONICALLY by model_family()'s own output (no new naming scheme): `claude-sonnet` is one entry whose `ids` map rail → the id that rail is asked for, so a `modelDeny` of the canonical key binds across every rail serving it (the Goal's acid test) and the M11 cross-rail ladder can say 'cheapest rail serving X'. `tier` is the retired `model_tiers` grade (the human-approved universe — graduation stays human); `context_tokens` is the per-model harness window (today the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS constant in agents/agent-session.sh, deleted there by theme 3 — DECLARED here so /route and /router-status can echo it); `tool_verified` is the date the model was verified to complete a tool-call loop through our stack (null = not yet declared); `pool_usd` is the Go rail's per-model monthly pool (gometer's '$NN pool'), null on every other rail. A `:free`/`:exacto` VARIANT collapses into its family (model_family() drops the suffix), so the variant's own price is the price callback's job and its exclusion is `never_free`'s — never a second table row. Two CI asserts in router-self-test pin the table to the parser: for every entry and every (rail, id) under it, model_family(id) == key AND model_id.parse(id).rail == rail — so the table cannot drift from model_id.py. A null fact is 'not yet declared', never a guess.

class_floors._comment: M8 per-class eligibility floors vs the capability table (AA composite indices, proxy-pulled weekly via MCP list-benchmarks). PERMISSIVE: a model without data always passes - the floor acts only on evidence, so a data gap can never brick a chain. Router is AGENT_ROUTER=shadow fleet-wide until the P4 flip: floors show up in shadow decisions first; tighten with that evidence (FU-095).
